Hospital bills can be a huge financial burden, but they shouldn’t be. 

I recently sat down with officials from Gerald Champion Regional Medical Center in Otero County to discuss ways to support safety net hospitals and lower patient costs!

1 in 5 people are on Medicare in NM. 

I support expanding dental coverage for federal health programs, so I urged @CMSGov to expand medically necessary dental coverage for Medicare recipients.

New Mexico’s 2nd District is proudly rural but suffers from a tremendous shortage of healthcare professionals. 

That’s why this year, I led the bipartisan DOC Act & Rural Physician Workforce Act to address critical healthcare shortages from Lordsburg to T or C. https://t.co/1HTegKwI2D

During my visit to a La Clinica de Familia in Chaparral, I accepted the push-up challenge with a 79-year-old cancer survivor. 💪 

Funding for federally qualified healthcare centers, such as LCDF, will continue to provide quality health care in the colonias. https://t.co/L7Mxmt1AlQ
Teachers like Treva from Laguna Pueblo are the heart of Tribal communities, fostering resilience, empowerment and wellness. https://t.co/JcQ3Ha9clG

I hosted a Mental Health Roundtable with Valencia County Community Wellness Council, focusing on youth mental health services in rural areas. 

I’m proud to lead the Mental Health Services for Students Act to ensure students’ well-being remains a top priority. #MentalHealthMonth https://t.co/UZgm2PF6Xw

We must protect reproductive autonomy, not undermine it. I'm proud to advocate for IVF coverage for government workers and ensure everyone has an equal opportunity to start a family. https://t.co/FEQcwF0hE0

Tribal communities lack direct access to the Commodity Supplemental Food Program, which gives food to low-income seniors.

I introduced the Tribal Nutrition Sovereignty Act to make it easier for Tribes & Pueblos to benefit from the program, giving Tribal communities more sovereignty.

Today, I unfortunately tested positive for COVID-19 after experiencing COVID-like symptoms. I will continue working on behalf of New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District while I follow CDC guidelines and the directives of my doctor.

Too often, New Mexico veterans’ voices aren’t heard.

That’s why I asked @VetAffairsDems Ranking Member @RepMarkTakano to listen to NM’s vets and ensure that we are actively solving the chronic issues we continue to see across our providers, hospitals and CBOCs. https://t.co/WB4IW6s5W4

Great News! Starting this month, Medicare enrollees now pay less for 54 part B drugs. 

Over 822K people will save on meds for cancer osteoporosis & pneumonia after prices outpaced inflation. Let’s keep health care affordable!

Big news, New Mexico: for the first time, DACA recipients are eligible to enroll in ACA health coverage. 

If you or someone you know qualifies, visit https://t.co/KBEXlZuWZn to find a plan that works for you. Open enrollment ends January 15, don’t miss out!

Carlsbad LifeHouse was recently named New Mexico's top addiction treatment center in Newsweek's 2024 rankings. Their vital work brings hope and healing to our community, and I’m proud to have them serving our district. https://t.co/oSaEnolUQk

I'm voting NO on the Republican budget resolution, which seeks to increase your health care costs, eliminate medicaid coverage, and eliminate food assistance programs for New Mexicans. This is at the same time Republicans are trying to give away your tax payer dollars to rich millionaires and billionaires.

Standing ovation for cutting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. This means ripping away benefits that seniors and working families rely on. I won’t let Washington balance the budget on the backs of those who need it most.

Federal funding cuts are hurting access to critical care, and I heard that firsthand from the Presbyterian Medical Services’ health center in Deming. Clinics like this one are essential for families across New Mexico. Thank you to the healthcare providers who show up for our community every day.

Let me be clear about what's happening here in this committee. Republicans are taking $300B out of the hands of working hungry families while down the hall Republicans are cutting Medicaid and health care, all so that the majority can give more tax breaks to the wealthy. https://t.co/S6gwLFaRMB
My thoughts are with President Biden and his family during this difficult time. I’m wishing him strength, healing, and hope as he begins treatment. New Mexicans are keeping him in our prayers.

Republicans voted to take away healthcare and food assistance from millions of families, including over 218,000 people right here in New Mexico. Why? To pay for more tax breaks for billionaires. https://t.co/8AgqiCtkuh
My constituents are reaching out worth a clear message: They are angry that Republicans are taking away their healthcare. https://t.co/ykPlr3Z0iO

Republicans just passed a 1000-page bill in the dead of night that strips health care and takes food off the tables of New Mexicans—all to hand billionaires another tax break.

It will raise costs, close hospitals, and hurt our families.

I voted NO. New Mexico deserves better.

This National EMS Week, I’m sending my deepest thanks to the emergency medical professionals serving southern New Mexico. From rural clinics to border towns, your commitment saves lives every day. I’m fighting to protect access to Narcan and ensure you have the tools you need to keep our communities safe. Thank you for all you do.

I have proudly co-sponsored the Invest to Protect Act, which gives small police departments more resources for training, recruitment, and mental health services. Our officers deserve support to do their jobs safely and effectively in every community. https://t.co/zp9icqZlAW

I visited the New Mexico State Veterans' Home in Truth or Consequences to see the top-notch facilities our veterans enjoy thanks to investments from our state leaders. I also spoke with the mayors of Truth or Consequences and Elephant Butte and we discussed housing, health care, water issues and how to strengthen the local economy.
Sierra County is a jewel in the Southwest.

Rural hospitals like Socorro General are lifelines for Southern New Mexico. I sat down with physicians and hospital administrators to hear firsthand what's at stake: Medicaid cuts that could shutter their doors and make it harder for expectant mothers and babies to get care they need. We talked about the urgent need to protect Medicaid funding and keep rural hospitals open. If these services disappear, people will die, and surrounding communities will suffer.
